question: True or false: store surveys have found about a quarter of brands sold in two sizes charge more per gram for the bigger pack?
answer: True. Surveys of American supermarkets found these quantity surcharges on roughly 16% to 34% of brands sold in two or more sizes. Most shoppers believe the big pack is the economy size, so a shop can price against that belief. The price per kilo on the shelf label settles it in seconds.
move: Check the unit price; a rule of thumb is what sellers price against.
ask: Which shopping rule of thumb do I follow without ever checking the label?
trap: Trusting that the big pack is always the cheaper way to buy.
source: Sprott, Manning and Miyazaki, Journal of Marketing, 2003
reference: Sprott, Manning & Miyazaki, Grocery Price Setting and Quantity Surcharges, Journal of Marketing, 2003
